asserts: A trace with NO `redaction` key was recorded before the rule existed and holds the launching shell's environment exactly as it was, tokens and all -- so `info` says `redaction: none -- recorded before redaction existed; plaintext throughout` rather than printing nothing, because absence of the key is not absence of secrets and a silent reader would let a plaintext store read as a redacted one. That line is the ONLY thing such a trace prints differently: the `env:` field is the bare hash it always was, with no count and no parenthesis, because a trace that never ran the rule has no measured zero to report. A second vector rather than a second question on v42: one vector builds one meta, and the two facts here are two metas.

questions.ask: What does `info` say about a trace that carries no redaction record at all -- and does it still print the plain `env:` field it always printed?
expect_contains: redaction: none -- recorded before redaction existed; plaintext throughout
